mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 0.5% compresses discount rates and stimulates equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is at or below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals worsening labor market conditions, triggering a short-term S&P 500 sell-off over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and real consumption (RSAFS) signal a broad-based demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS decline from prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline from prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In a recession, a monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates deteriorating economic activity, causing a short-term S&P 500 sell-off over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO declines from prior month during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts above 500,000 units (annualized) signals a strengthening housing sector, typically leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of periods when HOUST exceeds 500,000 units.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate falling below 0.5% signals aggressive monetary easing, boosting equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS falls below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment (UNRATE) and decline in employment (PAYEMS) signals severe labor market deterioration, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS declines from prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises and PAYEMS declines from prior month.

mechanism_narrative: During a recession, a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market recovery, typically preceding positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE declines from prior month during a recession.
